clues: The bag need not be sealed at the bottom: the pressure inside matches the air outside
The opening nearest the flame is made of a fire-resistant material such as Nomex
The first free human flight rose over Paris on 21 November 1783
Burning propane warms the air inside until it is lighter than the air outside
A wicker basket hangs beneath a great fabric envelope of warmed air

explanations: The envelope does not have to be sealed at the bottom, because the air inside is at about the same pressure as the air around it.
In modern sport craft the envelope is nylon and the inlet, closest to the burner flame, is a fire-resistant material such as Nomex.
The first untethered manned flight was made over Paris on 21 November 1783 by Pilâtre de Rozier and d'Arlandes, in a craft built by the Montgolfier brothers.
An open flame, usually burning liquid propane, heats the air inside, and the warm air is buoyant because it is less dense than the cold air outside.
It is a lighter-than-air aircraft: an envelope of heated air with a gondola or wicker basket slung beneath it.

sources.excerpt: The envelope does not have to be sealed at the bottom, since the air inside the envelope is at about the same pressure as the surrounding air.
In modern sport balloons the envelope is generally made from nylon fabric, and the inlet of the balloon (closest to the burner flame) is made from a fire-resistant material such as Nomex.

The first untethered manned hot air balloon flight in the world was performed in Paris, France, by Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier and François Laurent d'Arlandes on November 21, 1783, in a balloon created by the Montgolfier brothers.

Suspended beneath is a gondola or wicker basket (in some long-distance or high-altitude balloons, a capsule), which carries passengers and a source of heat, in most cases an open flame caused by burning liquid propane. The heated air inside the envelope makes it buoyant, since it has a lower density than the colder air outside the envelope.
A hot air balloon is a lighter-than-air aircraft consisting of a bag, called an envelope, which contains heated air.
